description: Maps each DB-stored scenario (by exact title) to the curated deck-side narrative shown to Wiley: the named deck scenario, the synthesised consensus percentage, and the primary signal. The DB scenarios are the canonical evidence base; this overlay provides the public-facing framing.

peer_review_under_strain.primary_signal: Entrenched weaknesses in peer review and editorial oversight are expected to drive higher retraction rates and undermine the credibility of leading journals.
peer_review_under_strain.minority_view: A subset expects incremental reforms or stabilization will prevent systemic collapse before 2030.

decision_fork.favorable: If systemic reforms and vetting controls are implemented quickly: leading journals stabilize credibility and moderate retraction rates.
decision_fork.adverse: If inertia persists and review fatigue deepens: reputational damage accelerates, driving researchers and funders toward alternative dissemination platforms.

action_windows.0_6_months: Audit current exposure to peer review risk and retraction trends
action_windows.6_18_months: Engage with or support reform alliances and technology pilots

public_trust_erosion_restoration.deck_scenario_name: Erosion and Restoration of Public Trust in Expertise
public_trust_erosion_restoration.primary_signal: Widespread skepticism toward health authorities and scientific expertise will define the late 2020s, but radical transparency and open data initiatives could restore legitimacy in the late 2030s.
public_trust_erosion_restoration.minority_view: A minority anticipates persistent distrust and fragmented public discourse despite transparency reforms.

decision_fork.favorable: If transparency reforms are fully realized: trust rebounds, enabling agencies like WHO, CDC, and EMA to reassert expert authority and public engagement.
decision_fork.adverse: If transparency remains partial or performative: distrust persists, fueling alternative knowledge networks and eroding compliance with public health guidance.

action_windows.0_6_months: Map trust levels and identify transparency gaps
action_windows.6_18_months: Pilot or advocate for open-data, open-review initiatives

ai_driven_reform.deck_scenario_name: AI-Driven Reform of Peer Review and Research Integrity
ai_driven_reform.primary_signal: By late 2030s, automation - driven by large language models and continuous validation - will become the dominant force in fraud detection and peer review, dramatically reducing misconduct and accelerating publication cycles.
ai_driven_reform.minority_view: Some stakeholders warn that algorithmic bias and lack of transparency could undermine AI credibility in evaluation.

decision_fork.favorable: If AI deployment is coupled with transparent oversight: leading publishers and research funders (NIH, Wellcome Trust) realize substantial gains in efficiency and reliability.
decision_fork.adverse: If AI is poorly governed or overly opaque: legitimacy crises accelerate, and regulatory backlash slows adoption or fragments standards across geographies.

action_windows.0_6_months: Review AI pilot participation and vendor partnerships
action_windows.6_18_months: Develop or support governance frameworks for algorithmic integrity

hybrid_decentralized_platforms.deck_scenario_name: Emergence of Hybrid and Decentralized Knowledge Platforms
hybrid_decentralized_platforms.primary_signal: Hybrid peer review - combining open commentary, automated checks, and decentralized collaboration - will test new trust mechanisms, diminishing the gatekeeping role of legacy publishers.
hybrid_decentralized_platforms.minority_view: Some expect traditional publishers to retain dominance via regulatory capture or proprietary standards.

decision_fork.favorable: If hybrid and decentralized models prove reliable and scalable: major publishers (Wiley, Elsevier) face accelerated disintermediation as researchers and funders migrate to open platforms.
decision_fork.adverse: If incumbent publishers successfully adapt or defend regulatory moats: market power consolidates around a few global players, with selective adoption of open or hybrid features.

action_windows.0_6_months: Track pilot projects and institutional migration patterns
action_windows.6_18_months: Establish partnerships with emerging platforms or invest in hybrid review capabilities

regulatory_response_reform.primary_signal: Governments and international bodies will introduce stringent publishing ethics frameworks and accelerate reform movements, reshaping research governance and compliance standards.
regulatory_response_reform.minority_view: Some expect regulatory action will be fragmented or insufficient, allowing misconduct to persist.

decision_fork.favorable: If reform coalitions and regulatory bodies coordinate effectively: global standards harmonize, reducing misconduct and restoring confidence among stakeholders.
decision_fork.adverse: If reforms are piecemeal or resisted: patchwork regulations create uneven compliance burdens and perpetuate vulnerabilities in research integrity.

action_windows.0_6_months: Map regulatory exposure and monitor legislative signals
action_windows.6_18_months: Align compliance frameworks and engage in reform advocacy
